'''Sivasspor Kulübü''', known as '''Kiğılı Sivasspor''' for sponsorship reasons,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sivas.bel.tr/sivassporun-isim-ve-forma-gogus-sponsoru-ozbelsan-as-oldu |title=Sivasspor'un İsim ve Forma Göğüs Sponsoru Özbelsan A.Ş. Oldu |publisher=Sivas Municipality |date=12 August 2025 |access-date=10 February 2026 |language=tr}}</ref> is a Turkish professional sports club based in [[Sivas]]. The club's primary department is men's football, which currently competes in the [[TFF 1. Lig|1. Lig]], the second tier of the Turkish football league system, following their relegation from the [[Süper Lig]] at the end of the 2024–25 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tff.org/Default.aspx?pageID=29&kulupID=3608 |title=Sivasspor Club Details |publisher=Turkish Football Federation |access-date=10 February 2026}}</ref>

The club was founded on 9 May 1967 through the merger of three local amateur clubs—'''Sivas Gençlik''', '''Yolspor''', and '''Kızılırmak'''—to meet the professional league requirements of the time.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sivasspor.org.tr/en/history/ |title=History of Sivasspor |publisher=Sivasspor Kulübü |access-date=10 February 2026}}</ref> Sivasspor plays its home matches at the [[New Sivas 4 Eylül Stadium]], which opened in 2016 and has a capacity of 27,532 spectators.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://stadiumdb.com/stadiums/tur/yeni_sivas_4_eylul_stadyumu |title=Yeni Sivas 4 Eylül Stadyumu (Sivas Arena) |publisher=StadiumDB |access-date=10 February 2026}}</ref> The team's traditional kit colors are red and white, representing the Turkish flag and the club's national identity.

Sivasspor experienced its most successful era in the Süper Lig during the late 2000s and early 2020s. They competed for the league title in two consecutive seasons, finishing fourth in [[2007–08 Süper Lig|2007–08]] and finishing as runners-up in [[2008–09 Süper Lig|2008–09]], their highest-ever league placement. The club is notable for being one of only three non-champion clubs (along with [[Altay S.K.|Altay]] and [[Kocaelispor]]) to have topped the Süper Lig standings at the halfway point of the season, a feat they achieved in 2007–08, 2008–09, and [[2019–20 Süper Lig|2019–20]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dailysabah.com/sports/football/sivasspor-finish-super-lig-first-half-atop-standings |title=Sivasspor finish Süper Lig first half atop standings |newspaper=Daily Sabah |date=29 December 2019 |access-date=10 February 2026}}</ref>

In domestic cup competitions, Sivasspor won their first major trophy by defeating [[Kayserispor]] 3–2 in the final of the [[2021–22 Turkish Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/en/sports/sivasspor-win-2022-turkish-cup/2600063 |title=Sivasspor win 2022 Turkish Cup |agency=Anadolu Agency |date=27 May 2022 |access-date=10 February 2026}}</ref> This victory qualified them for European competition, where they reached the Round of 16 in the [[2022–23 UEFA Europa Conference League]], eventually losing to [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]]. The club shares a fierce regional rivalry with Kayserispor, known as the "Central Anatolian Derby"."}}
